title: Law360 examines whether law firm partnerships are built for the modern market
summary: Law360 examines how evolving law firm ownership and compensation models are reshaping incentives across the legal industry. The article highlights growing debate around whether traditional partnership structures remain well-suited to long-term growth and value creation. Learn more.
body_markdown:
Law360 examines how evolving law firm ownership and compensation models are reshaping incentives across the legal industry. The article highlights growing debate around whether traditional partnership structures remain well-suited to long-term growth and value creation.


As quoted in the piece, Chief Operating Officer[Travis Lenkner](https://www.burfordcapital.com/about-us/our-team/travis-lenkner/) asserts that "the partnership structure is increasingly outmoded in today's competitive landscape" and suggests that alternative ownership models could better align incentives across firms.


Read the full article[here](https://www.law360.com/articles/2484325?ts_pk=304fc390-859f-4db7-a8fc-af00dcceab40&utm_source=user-alerts&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=tracked-search-alert&read_main=1&nlsidx=0&nlaidx=0) .
